conviction_note: No option anchor and no usable reaction history, so the number is built bottom-up: a first-ever 2026 P&L that resets earnings power against a still-quoted 3.0x trailing P/E (-3.0), a Sept 15 dilution vote and an Oct 1 de-SPAC lock-up expiry 12 trading days out (-1.5), an interim-CFO/dark-quarter disclosure record (-1.0), partly offset by BTC being +35% off the 30 June trough the release will report (+1.5).

findings.finding: CoinShares' own US ETF (BRRR) 10-Q puts bitcoin at $58,391 on 30 June 2026 vs $87,650 on 31 Dec 2025 (-33.4%) and BRRR net assets down 32.3% despite net creations, so group gross AUM of $7.4bn at FY2025 falls to roughly $5bn at 30 June; at the disclosed blended 170bp yield that is ~$50m of H1 asset-management revenue against $126.4m for FY2025, i.e. an annualised run-rate that turns the 3.0x trailing P/E screeners still display on CSHR into roughly 12x.
findings.why_not_priced: There is no consensus to be surprised against: the only visible sell-side coverage is a single KBW initiation (Outperform, PT cut $9 to $7), and CoinShares has published no interim P&L covering any part of 2026 - the last hard number on the tape is the 1 May 2026 FY2025 release headlined 'Reflecting Continued Strong Growth'. If the earnings-power reset were priced, the stock would not still be carried at a 3.04 P/E and a 7.66% indicated yield on the retail data pages that most of a 202k-ADV de-SPAC's marginal buyers read, and the 20-day run-up would not be +5.0%.
findings.independence: The FY2025 release itself gives the $7.4bn AUM, $126.4m asset-management revenue and ~170bp blended yield used to convert the AUM decline into revenue: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2087587/000121390026050703/ea028870801ex99-1.htm (6-K, 2026-05-01). Note this same FY2025 document is also the source of the segment figures in finding 2 - treat the two as one source cluster on that document, with the BRRR 10-Q the independent leg here.

findings.finding: Capital Markets - 37% of FY2025 revenue and gains ($73.1m) but 44% of segment EBITDA ($57.7m of $131.3m) - is the one line that cannot be reconstructed from the monthly AUM CoinShares publishes, and its largest single component was disclosed as ETH staking at $4.3m in Q2 2025 alone, a line that scales with token price and with a futures basis that compressed through a half in which industry ETP AUM fell from ~$160bn in May to ~$141bn by 1 June on record outflows.
findings.why_not_priced: The sweep's own cheap read is that H1 fee revenue is reconstructable from published fund-flow data; that is exactly why the market will anchor on AUM and mis-size the half. A US investor modelling CSHR as an asset manager applies a fee rate to AUM and gets the smaller, more resilient half of segment EBITDA right and the larger, regime-dependent half wrong. If this were understood, the name would not be quoted on a trailing P/E at all and the 63% realised vol would already have an option chain around it rather than 368 total open interest.
findings.independence: The segment split it rests on comes from the FY2025 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2087587/000121390026050703/ea028870801ex99-1.htm, 2026-05-01), which is shared with finding 1; the Q2 2025 release and the fund-flow volume (https://researchblog.coinshares.com/volume-288-digital-asset-fund-flows-weekly-report-166b82513893, 2026-06-01) are the independent legs.

findings.finding: The lock-up agreed at listing expires 1 October 2026 - 12 trading days after this print - and the day after the print shareholders vote on a 2026 Equity Incentive Plan with an 11% initial pool plus up to 3% a year for 2027-2029 (up to ~20% of the 131.8m shares outstanding), while a co-founder/director's 10b5-1 plan starts selling in September and adds 1.5m shares of monthly diversification sales the moment the lock-up lifts.
findings.why_not_priced: The 1 October lock-up date appears nowhere in the wire copy on the print; it is a clause inside a trading-plan press release, and no earnings preview or calendar row carries it. The headline 11% pool has been on the tape since 24 August, but the configuration - last information event before the entire pre-deal register can sell, with a dilution vote wedged between the two - is a sequencing fact rather than a headline, and it caps the upside to any good print because holders who want out have 12 sessions to act. If the market had focused on it, CSHR would not have rallied 2.84% on the EGM notice day.
findings.independence: The EGM resolutions (25% buyback authority at $0.01-$20.00, 11% pool, 3% evergreen 2027-2029, 131.8m shares outstanding, record date 27 August) are a separate document: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CSHR/notice-of-virtual-extraordinary-general-meeting-of-coin-shares-plc-60dgtz7l5wya.html (2026-08-24), filed as a 6-K at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002087587/000121390026092804/ea0303148-6k_coinshares.htm.

findings.finding: Bitcoin is ~$78,800 on 8-10 September against the $58,391 close on 30 June that this release will report AUM at - a 35% recovery after the balance-sheet date - and the EGM the next morning asks for authority to buy back up to 25% of shares at $0.01-$20.00, giving management both a strong current-AUM update and a live capital-return lever to pair with a weak historical half.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced - the BTC chart is public and is most of why the 20-day run-up is +5.0% against a -10.7% five-day - which is why this is sized small and positive rather than large. What is not priced is that management chose to report the day before a vote it needs to win, which is the maximum-incentive configuration for pairing a weak H1 with a current-quarter AUM print and buyback language; nothing in the coverage of the 30 July 'confirms quarterly reporting cadence' release anticipates a buyback being signalled at the results rather than after the vote.
findings.independence: The 30 July release frames the EGM as buyback-flexibility driven and is a separate document: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/30/3335872/0/en/CoinShares-Confirms-Quarterly-Reporting-Cadence-Seeks-Shareholder-Approval-for-Buyback-Authority.html (2026-07-30). The 30 June bitcoin level comes from the BRRR 10-Q used in finding 1 - same source cluster for that leg.

findings.finding: Richard Nash has signed as 'Interim Chief Financial Officer' since the 20-F certification dated 30 April 2026 and is still 'Interim CFO' in the 8 September results notice - over five months with no permanent CFO named - while the company's own governance page lists him without the qualifier, and CoinShares issued no press release at all between 1 May and 21 July 2026 before publishing a release whose purpose was to confirm it would report quarterly.
findings.why_not_priced: A company does not put out a release confirming it intends to report quarterly unless it has been asked why it went quiet; that release, an eleven-week communications gap, and an interim finance chief presenting the issuer's first ever SEC-format interim accounts together raise the chance of a presentation the market cannot reconcile to the Swedish-era numbers. If this were priced there would be a permanent-CFO search story in the coverage and the governance page and the press releases would not disagree on the man's title.
findings.independence: The title in the 8 September notice is a different document: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/08/3358085/0/en/coinshares-announces-date-of-first-half-2026-financial-results.html (2026-09-08); the eleven-week gap is visible on https://investor.coinshares.com/press.

searched_and_found_nothing: CoinShares' own monthly AUM / net-flow tracker at investor.coinshares.com - the pages render client-side and returned no figures via fetch; the 30 June group AUM number could not be pinned to a company URL, so the AUM path is sourced from the BRRR 10-Q instead

A '£1.4bn CoinShares Physical AUM at 30 June 2026, -32% from £2.1bn' figure surfaced twice in search summaries but could not be traced to any primary URL and is in the wrong currency for this issuer - dropped rather than filed
Any short-seller report, activist letter or litigation against CoinShares in 2026
A CFO departure announcement or permanent-CFO search release - none exists; 'Interim' simply predates the listing
Q1 2026 interim report - none was ever published; the Nasdaq Stockholm delisting in March 2026 ended quarterly Swedish reporting before any 2026 period was reported
CoinShares hiring pages, app-store data and customer forums - not a meaningful surface for an ETP issuer
Form 4 clusters - CoinShares is a foreign private issuer, so Section 16 reporting does not apply and there is no Form 4 trail
Terms and price of the Bastion Asset Management acquisition completed 2 September 2026 - no consideration disclosed, and it closed after the reporting period so it cannot affect H1 numbers
Sell-side previews or published H1 2026 estimates beyond the single KBW initiation and its $9 to $7 target cut
baseline_tension: There is no skew and no implied move to agree or disagree with, and my net negative cuts mildly against the baseline's +4.99% 20-day run-up while agreeing with the -10.7% five-day - so this is a call on the print's content and its calendar position, not a restatement of a stock already beaten down.
